newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Randgold Resources ups stake in Mali mine.
newsitem.headline: Randgold Resources ups stake in Mali mine.

text.p: Randgold Resources said on Thursday it planned to exercise its option to acquire a further 31 percent of the Loulo gold project in Mali this month.
After exercising the option, the company will hold 51 percent of the project.
RR (Randgold Resources) acquired its existing 20 percent stake in Loulo along with the Syama gold mine and other properties when it bought BHP Minerals Mali Inc last year.
That transaction included the option to buy a further 31 percent which could be exercised upon the submission of a feasibility study and the payment of 18 million francs.

The company said the feasibility study had been completed and would be presented to the board of Somilo, the company which holds the rights to the Loulo project, and a Somilo shareholders meeting on June 18.

No decision to mine had been made but it was anticipated that RR unit Randgold Resources Mali Inc would make such a recommendation within the next month. On-site construction would begin in January subject to the necessary approval.

Initial mining operation would aim at milling a total of 120,000 tonnes of ore per month from two pits at Loulo and Yalea. Their combined gold production, utilising one processing plant, is planned to be 140,000 ounces of gold per year.
The other shareholders are the government of Mali and the company Mine Or, which will respectively contribute 16 percent and 15 percent of the 31 percent RR stake is to recieve.
